rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: If you rent in Los Angeles in a unit not covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, your landlord can evict you only for a listed at-fault or no-fault reason once you have lived there six months or your original lease has expired. For no-fault evictions, such as owner move-in or demolition, the landlord must pay relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 6 months' tenancy or lease expiration; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions

coverage.summary: Most residential rental properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and properties with only one single-family dwelling. It applies once the tenant has lived in the unit for six months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance abuse treatment centers
some properties owned by HACLA or the government

rules.exemptions: Units regulated by the RSO (which have their own protections), transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or treatment facilities, and some HACLA/government-owned properties.
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction: The page says single-family homes and condos exempt from state just-cause law (AB 1482) under the corporate-ownership and notice conditions are still covered by the JCO.

rules.title: Minimum rent arrearage (Fair Market Rent threshold) for nonpayment evictions
rules.requirement: In any RSO or JCO unit in Los Angeles, your landlord cannot evict you for falling behind on rent unless you owe more than one month's Fair Market Rent for your unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Arrears must exceed Fair Market Rent (by bedroom size)

coverage.summary: All RSO and JCO rental units in the City of Los Angeles.

rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).

rules.title: Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: Your landlord must file any eviction notice served on you with the Los Angeles Housing Department within three business days. You can check with LAHD whether your notice was filed.

coverage.summary: All JCO and RSO rental properties in the City of Los Angeles.

rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) statewide rent cap
rules.requirement: If your unit is more than 15 years old and not under local rent control, your annual rent increase is capped at 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower. Units already covered by Los Angeles's RSO follow the RSO instead.

coverage.summary: Residential units more than 15 years old (rolling), excluding units already subject to local rent control (LA RSO) and other listed exemptions.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: single-family homes and condominiums not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant was given written notice

rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years (rolling); deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties where the owner occupied the other unit for the entire tenancy; qualifying single-family homes and condos with written notice; units already subject to the RSO.
rules.quoted_span: rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower
rules.interaction: Units already subject to the City's RSO are not covered by AB 1482.

notes: The city page does not cite LAMC section numbers for the JCO, so citations use the ordinance name. The page gives AB 1482 caps for the LA region of 8.9% (Aug 2024 to Jul 2025) and 8.8% (Aug 2023 to Jul 2024), but no figure for the period covering the 2026-10-01 query date. The JCO's coverage of buildings newer than Oct 1, 1978 was not coded as a built_after cutoff, because the JCO also covers older non-RSO properties such as single-family homes. The registration and notice-posting requirements (Right to Counsel, Renters' Protections) were not extracted as separate rules.
